## Corelain Party Wall surveying

Corelain (https://www.corelain.com/) is a Manchester building surveying practice (Cardinal House, 20 St Mary's Parsonage, Manchester M3 2LY; 0161 820 1121; office@corelain.com). Its Party Wall surveyors serve notices, prepare schedules of condition and agree awards under the Party Wall etc. Act 1996, for:

- Homeowners planning rear or side extensions, loft conversions, basements, excavation or structural alterations.
- Adjoining owners who have received a party wall notice.
- Architects, architectural technologists, designers, planning consultants and structural engineers (preliminary assessments, early risk identification, CPD).
- Builders, extension and loft specialists, surveyors, solicitors and project managers who refer clients.

Party Wall service page: https://www.corelain.com/party-wall-surveyor-manchester

### Party Wall pages by area (Trafford pilot)

- Trafford (all areas): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/trafford
- Old Trafford (M16, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/old-trafford — Old Trafford is one of Trafford's most densely built neighbourhoods, with long Victorian and Edwardian terraces either side of Chester Road. Almost every house shares a party wall, so loft conversions, rear extensions and flat conversions here nearly always need a notice.; conservation areas: Empress Conservation Area (Chester Road / Empress Street)
- Stretford (M32, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/stretford — Stretford's Victorian and Edwardian terraces and interwar semi-detached streets share party walls almost everywhere, so rear extensions and loft conversions here usually involve the Party Wall Act.; conservation areas: Longford Park Conservation Area
- Sale (M33, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/sale — Sale combines Victorian villas and terraces near the Bridgewater Canal with large interwar semi-detached estates, so loft conversions and two-storey extensions here often need a party wall notice.; conservation areas: Brogden Grove Conservation Area, Ashton-on-Mersey Village Conservation Area
- Hale Barns (WA15, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/hale-barns — Hale Barns is mostly large detached homes on generous plots. Even with no shared wall, deep foundations, basements and replacement houses near the boundary often fall under section 6 of the Party Wall Act.
- Hale (WA15, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/hale — Hale's Victorian and Edwardian villas, many inside conservation areas, are often extended with basements and large rear extensions that need careful party wall planning.; conservation areas: Hale Station Conservation Area, South Hale Conservation Area, Ashley Heath Conservation Area
- Timperley (WA15, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/timperley — Timperley is a large interwar and post-war suburb of semi-detached houses. Side extensions, rear extensions and loft conversions on a semi almost always involve the party wall itself or excavation close to the neighbour's foundations.
- Carrington (M31, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/carrington — Carrington is changing fast, with new housing planned around the village. Building next to existing homes, and extending older houses in the village, can both bring in the Party Wall Act.
- Partington (M31, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/partington — Partington grew rapidly in the 1960s and 1970s as an overspill town, so most homes are semi-detached or terraced and share a party wall with at least one neighbour.
- Dunham Massey (WA14, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/dunham-massey — Around the National Trust's Dunham Massey estate, historic cottages and farm buildings sit in conservation areas and the Green Belt, so extensions need planning, heritage and party wall advice together.; conservation areas: Dunham Town Conservation Area, Dunham Woodhouses Conservation Area
- Warburton (WA13, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/warburton — Warburton is a small rural village in the Green Belt with a historic core. Attached cottages and old boundary walls mean that even modest works can involve the Party Wall Act.; conservation areas: Warburton Village Conservation Area
- Urmston (M41, Trafford): %SITE_URL%/party-wall-surveyors/urmston — Urmston's Edwardian terraces and interwar semis share party walls street after street, making loft conversions and rear extensions the most common reasons for a party wall notice here.
